messages:
sarah: Heads-up, found a plaintext PEM inside a partner-ingest S3 backup (staging). looks like an old KV export that includes wrapped blobs referencing a KMS key id. not public but accessible to a handful of infra jobs :eyes:
sec-bot: Alert: secret-scan detected potential secret in s3://redwood-partner-backups/staging/2026-03-22.tar.gz (rule: pem-private-key). opens at 4601234567
alex: @sarah can you paste the object path + sha? we need to triage exposure scope before rotating anything
sarah: path: s3://redwood-partner-backups/staging/2026-03-22.tar.gz sha256: d2f3...9b0. object owner: partner-ingest-service-account (svc-partner-ingest@redwood). looks like a full kv dump with fields: vault:ciphertext="projects/prod-kms/cryptoKeys/ingest-wrap/...", vault:path=secret/data/partner/staging
mike: prioritize containment: 1) revoke partner-ingest SA keys 2) revoke Vault wrap_token used by that SA (if any) 3) start targeted rotation for secrets in secret/data/partner/staging 4) enable audit logging export for vault/transit for 90d
jen: agree. also suggest a quick RBAC change: restrict partner-ingest SA to read-only for specific prefixes and rotate its creds. I'll open a short-lived policy patch and tag it urgent
pete: I'll run a blast-radius query across logs to find any access to that object: aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-partner-backups --prefix staging/ --query "Contents[?contains(Key, '2026-03-22')].{Key:Key}" ; then check CloudTrail for GetObject by that SA
sarah: doing quick grep on the extracted tar: found ~20 keys, most look like wrapped ciphertext, 2 entries include plaintext PEMs under author_pgp_key and deploy_key fields. adding sample (redacted):

-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIE...REDACTED...
-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----

mike: urgent checklist: - rotate any vault secrets referenced - rotate any KMS keys if wrap material was exposed - mark partner ingests as compromised and force token invalidation - notify partner security (template ready)
alex: tag:incident/secrets-leak. can infra temporarily remove partner-ingest SA from production queues? we can fail-open to fallback queue to avoid data loss
jen: I'll push a policy patch to restrict SA and open a PR for emergency RBAC rollback. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/9999 (WIP)
pete: audit logs: found two GetObject calls from a thirdparty IP on 2026-03-22 03:12 UTC using the partner-ingest-SA creds. escalated to network team for source validation and partner notification
sarah: action owner list: Sarah (evidence + object hashes), Mike (rotation coordination + KMS consult), Jen (RBAC change + PR), Pete (log sweep + partner notif), Alex (oncall ops + deploy isolation). I'll start a short incident doc and tag sec@ for SLA
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0316-23 (severity: medium). playbook: secrets-leak-vault-kms. assigned: mike, jen
alex: note — check Vault's wrapping token TTLs: if wrapping keys were brokered via ephemeral tokens we can reduce rotation scope. mike, can you validate with vault/transit team?
mike: on it. early estimate: 6-8 services require rotation; KMS key rotate is heavier (multi-region). if wrap material was exposed we may create a new key and rewrap ciphertexts from Vault transit (avoid mass decrypt)
jen: putting a temporary allowlist on vault-access -> partner-staging namespace for admin ops only. will revert after PR merge and verify audit entries
sarah: will send partner notice draft to #customer-success for review before sending. includes remediation steps and timeframe (48h for rotation, 72h for audit review)
alex: good. once we have rotation / RBAC PRs merge, let's run a post-rotation eval against the prompt-set that uses those secrets to ensure no regression (re: Redwood Optimize)
mike: timeline: containment within 2h, rotation start within 6h, full audit handoff in 72h. updating INC-2026-0316-23 with timestamps
sarah: thanks everyone. small note: avoid posting raw keys here. use secure incident doc. :lock:
